sentences.text: Misc. Appeal No. 5474 of 2022

Smt. Nirmala And Others
 Versus
 Narayan And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Chandra Prakash Purohit, learned counsel for t  Ms. Bhagyashree Gupta, learned counsel for the resp  ORDER

The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 31.03.2022 passed in claim case No.2659/2019.
2.
The factum of accident and liability of insurance company is not under dispute.

3. The short facts of the case are that on 01.12.2019 the husband of the appellant No.1-Naanuram was taking his son and daughter by his motorcycle bearing registration number MP09-MD-6072 from village- Naaded to New Mhow towards Palasiya and when he reached near Bherulal Patidar College, in front of shop of Ishwar Seth, Car No.MP09-CN-9965 coming from the side of Manpur being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of another person namely Mahesh from the front.
This accident resulted in the cascading accident with the motorcycle of the 2 MA-5474-2022 deceased bearing registration No.MP09-ND-7136 and the deceased Naanuram died.
The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for the compensation of death of Mahesh in the above said accident.
The claims tribunal considering the evidence on record awarded a total sum of Rs.13,77,000/-.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the income of the deceased- Naanuram has been assessed incorrectly.
He submits that the deceased was earning Rs.8000/- per month.
The claims tribunal did not accept the claim of the appellant for the reason that there was no material at all to support the claim of income of the deceased as Rs.8000/- per month.
Thus, the claims tribunal has taken the income of the deceased on notional basis as Rs.6000/- per month by treating him an unskilled labourer.
He further submits that there was no material contrary to the claim of the appellant regarding income of the deceased.
He further submits that even for future prospects an addition of 25% was made whereas it should have been made at 40% in view of the fact that the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
He further submits that even in other heads also less amount of compensation has been awarded.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company submits that just and proper compensation has been awarded.
The deceased was 40 years, thus, future prospects have rightly been added at 25%.

He also submits that in other heads proper compensation has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
6.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

On perusal of the record, it is seen that the claims tribunal has correctly disbelieved the claim regarding income of the deceased Naanuram as there was no concrete material to establish the assertion regarding earning Rs.8000/- per month.
As regards the future prospects, it is seen that claimants have stated that the deceased was less than 40 years of age even the claims tribunal has considered the age of the deceased as 40 years.
In such circumstances, future prospects should have been added at 40%.
Apart from this, even on notional basis, income at Rs.6000/- for unskilled labour at the time of accident appears to be less, the date of accident is 01.12.2019.
But, looking to the facts of the case, this Court is not inclined to re-quantify the entire amount of compensation.
In the fitness of things, this Court deems it fit to award a lump-sum amount of Rs.2,00,000/-.
This amount shall be over and above the amount which has already been awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% from the date of application presented before the claims tribunal.
8. In view of the above, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
